brief: J.P. Morgan estimates the S&P500 equity risk premium, the gap between its modelled equity discount rate and the 10y real UST yield, has fallen to 2.1%, below the 2.4% Q3 2007 cycle low and the lowest since 2002, driven by the equity rally plus the further rise in real bond yields. Three consequences follow. Equities become more sensitive to bond yields, as in the low-premium 1974-1998 period. Long-term investors, already the most overweight equities versus bonds since 2002, gain an incentive to rebalance into bonds. The positive bond-equity correlation in place since 2022 is reinforced, a headwind for risk parity that raises demand for direct equity put hedges. The low premium can in principle persist if AI productivity gains lift earnings growth. On rates, the DKW model decomposition shows the 2022 repricing was largely expected real short rates, while the rise since late Feb26 splits roughly evenly between expected short rates and term premia, consistent with higher perceived potential growth, with fiscal dynamics and DM QT also contributing. Pivotal Path preliminary data show hedge funds returned 1.4% in August, reversing July, but Equity Sector TMT recaptured only a third of its July loss.

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan estimates the S&P 500 equity risk premium has declined to 2.1%, its lowest level since 2002.
cards.anchor: the S&P500 Equity Risk Premium has currently declined to only 2.1% on our estimates, its lowest level since 2002

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan had argued last May that the S&P 500 equity risk premium had already breached the previous cycle low of 2.4% seen in Q3 2007.
cards.anchor: had already breached the previous cycle low of 2.4% seen in Q3 2007

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan puts equity risk premia at roughly 2%, 100bp below historical averages.
cards.anchor: the shrinkage of Equity Risk Premia towards 2%, 100bp below historical averages

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan expects equity markets to show higher sensitivity to bond yields going forward than over the past two decades, drawing on the low equity risk premium period of 1974-1998.
cards.anchor: going forward equity markets could exhibit higher sensitivity to bond yields

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan's asset allocation metrics show investors are the most overweight equities versus bonds since 2002.
cards.anchor: investors are currently very overweight equities vs. bonds, the most overweight since 2002

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan expects the compressed equity risk premium to give multi-asset investors an incentive to raise bond allocations, making rebalancing flows out of equities into bonds more pronounced than in recent years.
cards.anchor: with an incentive to increase bond allocations going forward

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan expects greater equity sensitivity to bond yields to reinforce the positive bond-equity correlation that emerged in 2022.
cards.anchor: higher sensitivity of equity markets to bond yields going forward would reinforce the positive

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan expects a sustained positive bond-equity correlation to be a more lasting headwind for the risk parity trade, which relies on bond duration as a hedge to equity risk.
cards.anchor: could create a more sustained headwind for the so-called “risk parity trade”

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan expects multi-asset investors to increase demand for direct equity market hedges such as equity puts.
cards.anchor: equity market hedges such as equity puts by multi-asset investors

cards.claim: J.P. Morgan says the current lower equity risk premium can in principle be sustained if AI-related productivity gains boost earnings growth.
cards.anchor: lower risk premium can in principle be sustained e.g. if AI-related productivity gains provide a boost

cards.claim: The DKW model decomposition shows the rise in 10y real US Treasury yields since late February 2026 has been split roughly evenly between expected real short rates and real term premia.
cards.anchor: the rise in real rates has been roughly evenly split between expected real short rates and term premia

cards.claim: The 2022 repricing of real US yields was largely driven by a repricing of real expected short rates rather than term premia.
cards.anchor: sharp repricing of real rates in 2022 was largely driven by a repricing of real expected short rates

cards.claim: Consensus long-term US growth expectations have improved since late 2023, which J.P. Morgan says could mean part of the recent rise in real rates reflects optimism over the AI investment cycle, with fiscal pressures a potential contributing factor.
cards.anchor: long-term growth expectations have begun to improve, suggesting that some of the rises in real rates recently could reflect optimism

cards.claim: Preliminary Pivotal Path data show hedge funds returned 1.4% in August 2026, fully reversing the July loss.
cards.anchor: hedge funds returned 1.4% in August, fully reversing the July loss

cards.claim: Equity Sector TMT hedge funds recaptured only a third of their July loss in August, which J.P. Morgan reads as July deleveraging still weighing on them.
cards.anchor: Equity Sector TMT hedge funds lagged by recapturing only a third of the July loss

cards.claim: Discretionary Macro hedge funds and CTAs both returned above 2% in August 2026, more than reversing their July loss.
cards.anchor: Both Discretionary Macro hedge funds and CTAs returned above 2% in August

cards.claim: The implied equity beta of Discretionary Macro hedge funds rose markedly in August, pointing to an increase in their equity exposure.
cards.anchor: The implied equity beta of Discretionary Macro hedge funds increased markedly in August

cards.claim: The implied equity beta of Equity Long/Short hedge funds stood above average levels in August 2026.
cards.anchor: The implied equity beta of Equity Long/Short hedge funds also stood above average levels in August
